value.behaviour: Writes a line with styled runs as one <text> of <tspan>s with highlight rects behind it; every other line stays byte for byte.
rules: On a line with no styled run, the existing textContent, attribute order and append order stay as they are.
Colours reach the SVG through setAttribute only.

sites.rule: Add `import { getStyledTextLines, layoutTextStyleRuns } from "@excalidraw/element";`.
Add `const styledLines = getStyledTextLines(element);`.
Add `const runs = styledLines?.[i];` and set textContent only when runs is falsy.

When runs is truthy, loop over layoutTextStyleRuns(element, lines[i], runs, renderConfig.renderEnvironment). For a run with highlight, create an SVG_NS rect with x, y = i * lineHeightPx, width, height = lineHeightPx, and fill = applyDarkModeFilter(run.highlight, renderConfig.theme === THEME.DARK), and append it to node. Then create an SVG_NS tspan with textContent = lines[i].slice(run.start, run.end), set its fill to applyDarkModeFilter(run.color, same theme test) only when run.color is set, and append it to text. Keep `node.appendChild(text);` last, so the rects sit behind the text.

sites.rule: Keep the three imports and add isTextElement, mergeTextStyles and noteMergedTextStyles.

Add `const mergeStyleRanges = <T extends OrderedExcalidrawElement>(winner: T, loser: OrderedExcalidrawElement, localElement: OrderedExcalidrawElement): T`, with a doc comment that the text still has one winner and only its ranges merge. Return winner unless winner and loser are both text elements. merged = mergeTextStyles(winner, loser). If merged !== localElement and localElement is text, call noteMergedTextStyles(localElement, merged). Return merged.

The discard branch pushes mergeStyleRanges(localElement, remoteElement, localElement); this also covers the mid-edit discard. The other branch pushes localElement ? mergeStyleRanges(remoteElement, localElement, localElement) : remoteElement. The added.add calls stay as they are.

sites.rule: Add `getTextStyleRuns,` to the import.
Change to `onChange?: (data: { nextOriginalText: string; caret: number }) => void;`.

Add `let styleOverlay: HTMLDivElement | null = null;` and `let overlayContent: { text: string; ranges: ExcalidrawTextElement["textStyleRanges"]; isDark: boolean } | null = null;`, then `const syncStyleOverlay = (textElement: ExcalidrawTextElement) => {...}` with a doc comment that a textarea cannot draw coloured runs, so a layer behind it does. Steps: 1. ranges = textElement.textStyleRanges. If there are none: remove the overlay and reset it and overlayContent to null, remove class excalidraw-wysiwyg--styled, remove the caret-color property, and return. 2. Create the overlay when missing: an ownerDocument div with class excalidraw-wysiwyg-styles, aria-hidden true and dir auto, added with editorBox?.prepend(overlay). 3. Read baseColor = editable.style.color, set overlay.style.cssText = editable.style.cssText, then Object.assign pointerEvents none, userSelect none and unicodeBidi plaintext onto overlay.style. 4. Set editable.style.caretColor = baseColor, editable.style.color = transparent, and add class excalidraw-wysiwyg--styled. 5. isDark = app.state.theme === THEME.DARK. Return if overlayContent has the same text (editable.value), the same ranges reference and the same isDark. 6. Otherwise overlay.replaceChildren(), and for each run of getTextStyleRuns(editable.value, 0, ranges): text = value.slice(run.start, run.end); a run with no colour appends a text node; a styled run appends a span with textContent = text, style.color from applyDarkModeFilter(run.color, isDark) when set, style.backgroundColor from applyDarkModeFilter(run.highlight, isDark) when set. Then store overlayContent.
Add `syncStyleOverlay(updatedTextElement);`. The style assignment above has just reset editable.style.color to the base colour.
Change to `onChange({ nextOriginalText: editable.value, caret: editable.selectionEnd });`, formatted by Prettier.
